content: Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information about this medication and your specific health needs. Hyoscyamine, commonly sold under brand names such as Hyosyne and Levsin, is used to treat various gastrointestinal conditions, including stomach cramps, infant colic, and irritable bowel syndrome. It is also prescribed for bladder and bowel control issues, cramping pain caused by kidney stones or gallstones, and symptoms associated with Parkinson's disease. This medication works by reducing stomach acid production, slowing gut movement, and relaxing muscles in organs such as the stomach, intestines, bladder, kidneys, and gallbladder. Additionally, it decreases the production of certain body fluids, such as saliva and sweat. To use this medication, take it orally as directed by your doctor, typically 30 to 60 minutes before meals. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also calculated based on weight. Do not increase your dose or take it more frequently than prescribed without consulting your doctor. Note that antacids can reduce the absorption of hyoscyamine. Common side effects may include dizziness, drowsiness, blurred vision, dry mouth, headache, difficulty sleeping, constipation, flushing, dry skin, and reduced sweating. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. Before taking hyoscyamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, atropine, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you have alcohol dependence or liver disease, use caution, as this medication may contain alcohol. Hyoscyamine can cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision, which may be worsened by alcohol or marijuana. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages, as this drug may increase the risk of heatstroke by reducing sweating. Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, such as confusion, drowsiness, unusual excitement, constipation, or difficulty urinating. During pregnancy, hyoscyamine should only be used when clearly necessary, as it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels of all your medications, as some may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. Hyoscyamine may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially leading to false results. If someone overdoses and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Managing digestive disorders may involve lifestyle changes, such as stress reduction programs, regular exercise, quitting smoking, and dietary adjustments to enhance the effectiveness of this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized information about this medication and your health needs.
